History:
- Presenting complaint: Progressive decreased hearing in the left ear for ~6 weeks.
- Symptom onset/duration/progression: Began ~6 weeks ago; intermittent symptoms throughout this period, some triggers noted (e.g., watching TV or listening to music alters the ringing).
- Associated symptoms: Intermittent left-sided tinnitus; several episodes of mild dizziness/feeling off-balance (not full rotational vertigo); occasional nausea related to dizziness.
- Prior similar episode: Brief hearing problem ~1 year ago that lasted a couple of days.
- Negative symptoms: No ear pain, no ear discharge, no documented fever, no chest pain, no palpitations.
- Social/contextual: Patient is able to attend face-to-face clinic; not an emergency.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic medical conditions documented in the transcript.
- No prior hospitalizations documented.
- Allergies: Not documented.
- Current medications: Not documented.
- Note: Patient response regarding use of cotton buds is unclear in the transcript (see Quality checks).

Physical Examination:
- No formal examination performed during this consult.
- Reported/observed findings: Decreased hearing localized to the left ear; tinnitus left-sided; right ear reported as normal by patient.
- Relevant negatives reported: No ear pain, no ear discharge, no fever, no chest pain, no palpitations.
- Mental status: Patient conversational and oriented during interview.
- Planned physical exam: Otoscopic examination of the ears recommended to exclude impacted cerumen or ear drum pathology.

Impression:
- Left-sided hearing impairment with tinnitus and intermittent mild imbalance; need to exclude cerumen impaction or other ear/inner-ear pathology with otoscopic examination.

Management Plan:
- Arrange face-to-face clinic appointment within ~4–5 days for otoscopic examination by a GP to assess for impacted cerumen and ear drum/inner-ear pathology.
- Admin team to be contacted to slot patient into clinic; clinician to leave support-team contact number in the notes for patient to call to arrange appointment.
- Provide patient with a tinnitus information leaflet (link to be pasted into appointment notes) and advise patient to review it prior to the clinic visit.
- Advise patient not to use cotton buds to clean ears (clinician counseled against use).
- Safety-netting: If any problems or worsening symptoms before the clinic appointment, patient to book another appointment or contact the practice/support team; not currently considered an emergency.

Patient Summary:
- Patient reports ~6 weeks of reduced hearing in the left ear with intermittent left-sided tinnitus and mild imbalance. The clinician suspects common causes such as impacted cerumen and recommended an in-person otoscopic exam within 4–5 days. Educational material on tinnitus will be provided and the admin team will schedule the clinic visit.

Key Takeaways:
- Attend an in-person ear clinic appointment within ~4–5 days for otoscopic examination.
- Do not use cotton buds to clean the ears.
- Read the provided tinnitus information leaflet and contact the practice if symptoms worsen.

Next Steps:
- Otoscopic examination of both ears (focus left ear) at face-to-face GP clinic visit.
- If impacted cerumen is identified: removal/treatment as indicated during clinic visit.
- If ear is clear: further assessment of inner-ear/balance system and discussion of additional diagnostic steps (to be determined after examination).

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: vital signs, complete past medical history, allergy list, medication reconciliation, family history, smoking/alcohol history, neurological exam details, and audiology results (none documented in transcript).
- Internal conflicts noted: clinician addressed patient as "John" though patient identified as "Jack Smith"; patient response regarding use of cotton buds is unclear/conflicting in transcript.
- Transcript quality comment: Transcript is generally clear; occasional brief pauses and minor ambiguities (notably regarding cotton bud use and the clinician's use of an incorrect name). No major audio incomprehensibility evident.
